ET-M4-1.statement: Drone episodes are imported read-only through the contract and validate.
ET-M4-1.sources: only banshee's published exports, each with MANIFEST.json and COMPLETE: first the existing D1 episodes, then a variation set. Nothing is imported from an export before its COMPLETE exists, and no consumer-side manifest is built. banshee is never written to.
ET-M4-1.scope: every episode listed in either export's MANIFEST.json, from both stacks, including failed, trial, superseded and re-recorded runs. No runs-of-record or other selection from banshee's reports or ledgers is applied.
ET-M4-1.schema_check: the top-level schema_version of each MANIFEST.json, and each episode's own schema_version, must be 1.0.0, the contract schema_version that the pinned ironclad-kit v1.2.0 validates (ironclad docs/adr/ADR-0008-PROGRAM-schema-version-decides-exchange.md). If it is missing, differs, or the manifest declares more than one schema version, stop and report before copying.
ET-M4-1.validator: vishwaroop's pinned ironclad-kit v1.2.0, from vishwaroop's own tooling environment. banshee's installed code is never run.
ET-M4-1.threshold: 100% of imported episodes contract_valid, and every copied file's sha256 equal to the producer manifest's
ET-M4-1.metadata: each episode keeps its original metadata unchanged, including split.partition dev. The stack (ROS 2 Jazzy or Humble) is recorded as a field of the import record; it is not a family or partition key.
ET-M4-1.ulogs: the raw ULogs are a separate read-only import: their sha256 is checked against the producer manifest, they are not contract records, they are outside ET-M4-1's count, and ET-M4-2 does not use them

ET-M4-2.statement: The residual model predicts 1 s of open-loop motion better than the nominal model on held-out flight families.
ET-M4-2.data_checks_before_any_fit: ET-M4-2's nominal fit, any training, and scoring happen only after both exports are imported, validated and checked, over their union. Before any of them: (1) every episode_id occurs once across both exports with one family, and no transitions-file sha256 occurs in more than one family; (2) every family belongs to exactly one M4 partition across both exports; (3) the manifests designate exactly one partition for training and exactly one for held-out evaluation; (4) every episode's action_spec labels are [ve, vn, vu, yaw_rate] with units [m/s, m/s, m/s, rad/s], and its 'state' stream has frame enu_local and 7 values. If any check fails, stop and report.
ET-M4-2.families_and_partitions: A family is the producer manifest's family identifier, or its (route, wind, fault) triple if no identifier is given; each identifier maps to exactly one triple and back. A family's M4 partition is the one the producer manifests' family plan assigns. It is a separate field from each episode's split.partition, which stays dev, is kept unchanged, and plays no part in choosing training or held-out data. Families in any partition other than training and held-out are not used by ET-M4-2.
ET-M4-2.rollout: Open loop for 20 steps (1 s at 20 Hz), from the true state, driven by the logged velocity setpoints. The true state is the logged contract 'state' observation (PX4's estimate), both as every window's start and as every target; no ULog, Gazebo or outcome.json ground truth is used. Let s_0 be the state in transition t's observations. For j = 0 to 19, s_{j+1} = f(s_j, ...), with a_{t+j} = action.transmitted of transition t+j and dt_{t+j} = dt_ns of transition t+j in seconds. The prediction at step k (k = 1 to 20) is s_k and is compared with the state in next_observations of transition t+k-1. action.requested and action.filtered are never used. Both models score the same window list.
ET-M4-2.learned_model_inputs: for a window starting at t, only: the state observations of transitions t-3 to t, action.transmitted of transitions t-3 to t+19, the dt_ns of those transitions, and its own predictions within the window. No logged state after t, no context field, and no episode, family, fault, embodiment, stack, outcome or rubric metadata.

window_eligibility.candidates: every transition position t of an episode, ordered by step, for which positions t-3 and t+19 exist in that episode. An episode with fewer than 23 transitions has none and is reported as too short.
window_eligibility.rule: A candidate is eligible when transitions t-3 to t+19 have consecutive step numbers (g) and each of them has: (a) exactly one entry with stream 'state' in observations and exactly one in next_observations, each with valid true and exactly 7 finite values; (b) action.transmitted non-null with exactly 4 finite values, action.sent_t_ns non-null, and action.valid_until_t_ns >= t_ns + dt_ns; (d) 45,000,000 <= dt_ns <= 55,000,000; (e) the state's capture_t_ns in next_observations greater than in observations by at most 75,000,000 ns, and the next transition's observations carrying that same sample or a later one (a fresh sample every step, never a repeated or stale hold). Windows from failed flights are included. Interventions do not exclude a window. The 40-step reporting horizon uses the same rule over t-3 to t+39.
window_eligibility.reported: for each family: candidates, eligible windows, episodes contributing, episodes too short, and each excluded window counted once under its first failing reason in the order (g), (a), (b), (d), (e), plus the count failing each reason. Also, reported but not gated: the gated metric over eligible windows with context.intervention null throughout, and the count of eligible windows containing an intervention.
window_eligibility.stop: if any held-out family has no eligible window, stop and report

ET-M4-2.nominal_model: First-order velocity tracking with an integer input delay d and trapezoidal position integration, in ENU. With u_j = transmitted[0:3] = (ve, vn, vu) of transition t+j (j may be -1 to -3, which eligibility provides) and r_j = transmitted[3]: v_{j+1} = v_j + a (u_{j-d} - v_j) per axis, with a_h for the east and north axes and a_v for up; p_{j+1} = p_j + dt_{t+j} (v_j + v_{j+1}) / 2; yaw_{j+1} = wrap(yaw_j + dt_{t+j} r_{j-d}), with u applied to state indices 3, 4, 5 in order and r added to index 6 as logged. Fit on the M4 training partition only: a training transition i is usable when it alone meets (a), (b), (d) and (e), and so do transitions i-1 to i-3 for the delayed input. For each d in {0, 1, 2, 3}: with v_i from its observations, v_{i+1} from its next_observations and e_i = u_{i-d} - v_i, and no intercept, a_h = sum over usable i and axes E, N of (v_{i+1} - v_i) e_i / sum of e_i^2, and a_v the same over U alone. If a denominator is below 1e-9 (m/s)^2, stop and report. Each gain is clipped to [0, 1]. d is the value with the lowest sum of squared one-step velocity residuals over usable training transitions, ties to the smaller d. d, a_h and a_v are recorded, with the sha256 of the training-transition list, before any held-out family is scored.
ET-M4-2.learned_model: the nominal above plus a learned residual, trained on the training partition only. Its work order freezes, before any training, one configuration and its seeds (0, 1 and 2). Every choice (architecture, history use, normalization, epochs, early stopping, hyperparameters) is made on training-partition data only, by holding out training families. Each seed's prediction is its deterministic mean; an ensemble counts as one model, predicting its mean.
ET-M4-2.gated_metric: For each held-out family f: the mean, over its eligible windows, of the squared 3-D Euclidean position error at step 20. RMSE is the square root of the equal-weight mean of those family means.
ET-M4-2.threshold: pass if learned RMSE <= 0.85 x nominal RMSE for every declared seed (the worst seed decides). The owner's gate is the ratio; requiring it of every seed is the agent's stricter reading.
ET-M4-2.scored_once: one command fits or loads the nominal, builds the window list, writes its sha256, and scores the nominal and every declared learned seed on that list in the same run. It refuses to score the held-out families again once a result exists. A run that stops at a stop condition writes no score and may be repeated after the cause is reported. No other learned model, checkpoint or seed is scored on the held-out families for this test.
ET-M4-2.reported_not_gated: per-family scores and episode counts; velocity error at step 20 as the 3-D Euclidean norm of predicted minus logged (vx, vy, vz), in m/s, aggregated like position; yaw error at step 20 as wrap(yaw_pred - yaw_logged), with wrap(x) = ((x + pi) mod 2 pi) - pi, in rad, aggregated like position; the same three at step 40, over 40-step-eligible windows (a family without any is reported as such); a bootstrap with 10,000 resamples from numpy default_rng(0), in which each held-out family resamples its own episodes with replacement, each drawn episode bringing all its eligible windows, both models sharing each resample, giving the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of nominal RMSE, learned RMSE and their ratio; a family with fewer than 2 episodes is marked 'interval not estimable'; the gate ratio recomputed with each held-out family left out in turn. Flagged: every held-out family whose learned step-20 mean squared position error exceeds the nominal's; listed separately, every family where the learned model is worse on velocity or yaw at step 20, or on any metric at step 40.
